author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks in New Delhi on Friday, meeting shortly before India hosts the BRICS summit. Reuters reported that the agenda covered trade, energy and defense as well as civil nuclear cooperation, fertilizers, manufacturing, railways, steel and critical minerals.

The meeting was the leaders’ second in two weeks and underscored India’s effort to maintain strategic ties with Moscow despite Western sanctions tied to Russia’s war in Ukraine. Russian oil supplied a record 51% of India’s imports in July, although that share later eased as China increased purchases.

Modi reiterated India’s support for diplomacy to end the war and defended the country’s need for reliable energy supplies. The discussions also follow agreements reached during Putin’s December 2025 visit to deepen commercial and defense cooperation.

The talks are developing in the context of the BRICS gathering, where leaders from China and Iran are also expected. Their outcome could affect energy flows, defense procurement and coordination among member countries. Any concrete commitments will depend on formal announcements following the bilateral session and summit meetings.
dek: The leaders met in New Delhi to discuss energy, defense and industrial cooperation as India prepares to host the wider summit.
headline: Modi and Putin hold trade and defense talks before BRICS summit
